$description: conductor design tokens (Daylight) (W3C Design Tokens Format, 2025.10). Three tiers: primitive (raw values) → semantic (roles, per theme and density) → component (aliases of semantic). Mode-dependent tokens carry every mode in $extensions.mode (the Terrazzo convention); $value is the default (dark / comfortable / standard). Contrast intent is declared in $extensions["org.conductor.contrast"] and checked by tools/tokens.mjs.

color.$description: Raw palettes (Daylight). sand is the warm neutral ramp (50 lightest … 975 the logo ink); cream (light) and cocoa (dark) are six-step surface sets, 0 sunken · 1 canvas · 2 rail · 3 surface · 4 raised · 5 overlay. The hue ramps are 11-step OKLCH ramps, frozen. Components never use these directly.

975.$description: Logo ink on cream: deeper than body text so the mark holds at small sizes.

500.$description: Parked / idle: a cool grey, distinct from passed (green) and from ink.

600.$description: Passed: a quiet, muted green for the overwhelming majority of marks.

serif.$description: Display and brand: page titles, section titles, one hero number, the wordmark. Upright, never italic.

sans.$description: Everything people read and act on. Designed by the Braille Institute so easily confused characters stay distinct.

mono.$description: Only literal code, ids, YAML and logs.

out.$description: Default. Things arriving or responding: fast start, soft landing.

in-out.$description: Things moving from one place to another on screen.

sunken.$description: Wells: code blocks, track of a segmented control.

rail.$description: The navigation rail and top strip.

raised.$description: Selected rows and nav items, nested cards (elevation 2).

field.$description: Inside text inputs: sunken on dark, white on light.

tertiary.$description: Metadata, timestamps, hints, placeholders. The faintest text that still has to be read.

disabled.$description: Disabled controls only (WCAG 1.4.3 exempts them). Never for content.

accent.$description: Text-safe accent: links and accent-coloured words. Use this, not accent.default, for any text.

on-accent.$description: Text and glyphs on accent.default fills.

muted.$description: Decorative or secondary icons. Still 3:1 (non-text contrast).

control.$description: Edges that identify a control (inputs, checkboxes): 3:1 per WCAG 1.4.11.

ring.$description: 2px ring, 2px offset, on every focusable element.

default.$description: Fills that mean “you / act here”: primary button, needs-you count, the active nav bar, the logo dot. Never text on light: use text.accent.

active.$description: Pressed. On dark it steps lighter, so dark on-accent text keeps AA.

subtle.$description: Wash behind selected choices and the needs-you row.

hover.$description: Layered over any surface on hover.

pressed.$description: Layered over any surface while pressed.

success.$description: Done, passed, healthy. Passed is green: a small green dot (solid) and a green word (fg) in regular weight. It stays calm because only failures are bold, red, edged and listed first; rows are never tinted. Parked stays slate pause bars, so the two never share a hue or a shape.

fg.$description: The word “Passed” and other success text: green, regular weight.

bg.$description: Tinted wash behind a banner or a changed line in a diff. Never behind a status label or a row.

solid.$description: The passed mark (the small dot): green.

chart.$description: Passed runs in charts: softer than the mark, so a screen of passes reads calm and the rare red pops first. Light: color-mix(in srgb, green-600 85%, surface); dark: color-mix(in srgb, green-500 72%, surface), resolved here against bg.surface. Charts sit on a card (surface or raised): on the light canvas it is 2.98:1, below the 3:1 floor.

warning.$description: Needs attention soon, degraded, waiting on something. Glyph: triangle. Always pair with the glyph and a text label: colour alone never carries state.

bg.$description: Tinted wash behind a banner or a changed line in a diff. Never behind a status label or a row.

solid.$description: Dots, bars, timeline marks. Not for text.

danger.$description: Failed, refused, destructive. Glyph: cross. Always pair with the glyph and a text label: colour alone never carries state.

bg.$description: Tinted wash behind a banner or a changed line in a diff. Never behind a status label or a row.

solid.$description: The failed mark and the leading edge of a failed row. Chosen with tools/status-cvd.mjs to stay apart from passed (green) for colour-blind readers.

info.$description: Neutral news, updates, shadow mode (observes, never acts). Glyph: i in a circle. Always pair with the glyph and a text label: colour alone never carries state.

bg.$description: Tinted wash behind a banner or a changed line in a diff. Never behind a status label or a row.

solid.$description: Dots, bars, timeline marks. Not for text.

running.$description: In progress right now. Glyph: rotating arc (static under reduced motion). Always pair with the glyph and a text label: colour alone never carries state.

bg.$description: Tinted wash behind a banner or a changed line in a diff. Never behind a status label or a row.

solid.$description: Dots, bars, timeline marks. Not for text.

neutral.$description: Parked, idle, skipped, cancelled. A cool slate, never the warm ink of text, so parked never reads as passed or as plain metadata. Mark: pause bars (skipped: a dash).

bg.$description: Tinted wash behind a banner or a changed line in a diff. Never behind a status label or a row.

solid.$description: Dots, bars, timeline marks. Not for text.

code.$description: Syntax colours for YAML, JSON and logs, on bg.sunken.

add-mark.$description: The + gutter mark and change bar.

del-mark.$description: The − gutter mark and change bar.

dataviz.$description: Validated with the dataviz method (validate_palette.js) against bg.surface in both themes; see tokens/dataviz-validation.txt. Assign categorical slots in order, never cycled; fold a ninth series into “Other”. Scatter, maps and small multiples: at most three series.

sequential.$description: One hue (teal), light→dark for magnitude. Index 0 = least. Light: continuous scales (heatmaps) may use 0–8; ordinal ramps (tiers, stages) start at index 3 so the pale end still clears 2:1. Dark flips the ramp: index 0 is the darkest teal; ordinal ramps use 1–7.

diverging.$description: blue ↔ red with a neutral midpoint. Equal steps per arm. Use for deltas against a baseline (cost vs last week, p99 vs SLO).

now.$description: The “now” cursor: the only place the accent appears in a chart.

dot.$description: The 22px dot grid on the page background.

button.$description: The few button colours that differ by theme beyond the shared roles.

logo.$description: The logo’s ink. Deeper than body text on light so the mark holds its weight on cream; the dot always uses accent.default.

bot.$description: Bot identity colours: the fill behind a bot’s face or initials (drawn in ink), and a 3px rule on its chat messages. Never on status marks, buttons, links, counts, row edges, charts or text. Every hue keeps 20° clear of the status colours. Generated by tools/bot-palette.mjs.

rule.$description: The 3px rule on the bot’s own chat messages (olive): the other theme’s fill (deep in light, pastel in dark), so it shows at 3:1 on either page.

fg.$description: The face and initials on the olive fill: the theme’s ink.

rule.$description: The 3px rule on the bot’s own chat messages (lime): the other theme’s fill (deep in light, pastel in dark), so it shows at 3:1 on either page.

fg.$description: The face and initials on the lime fill: the theme’s ink.

rule.$description: The 3px rule on the bot’s own chat messages (teal): the other theme’s fill (deep in light, pastel in dark), so it shows at 3:1 on either page.

fg.$description: The face and initials on the teal fill: the theme’s ink.

rule.$description: The 3px rule on the bot’s own chat messages (lagoon): the other theme’s fill (deep in light, pastel in dark), so it shows at 3:1 on either page.

fg.$description: The face and initials on the lagoon fill: the theme’s ink.

rule.$description: The 3px rule on the bot’s own chat messages (plum): the other theme’s fill (deep in light, pastel in dark), so it shows at 3:1 on either page.

fg.$description: The face and initials on the plum fill: the theme’s ink.

rule.$description: The 3px rule on the bot’s own chat messages (rose): the other theme’s fill (deep in light, pastel in dark), so it shows at 3:1 on either page.

fg.$description: The face and initials on the rose fill: the theme’s ink.

rule.$description: The 3px rule on the bot’s own chat messages (stone): the other theme’s fill (deep in light, pastel in dark), so it shows at 3:1 on either page.

fg.$description: The face and initials on the stone fill: the theme’s ink.

shadow.$description: Warm, soft elevation. Light uses brown-tinted shadows; dark relies on the lighter surface step.

type.$description: Composite text styles (Daylight). Sizes in rem (1rem = 16px). Serif styles also set font-variation-settings (Fraunces’ soft axis).

display-xl.$description: Brand pages and the social card. Never in the dashboard.

h1.$description: Page titles: short and human (“Needs you”, “Activity”).

h2.$description: Card and section titles (“Needs you”, “Running now”). Short and human.

h3.$description: Item titles, dialog titles, and anything long or generated (“Replace the production web server”).

org.conductor.type.numeric: tabular-nums in tables, counters and timers; proportional in prose
tabular-nums in tables, counters and timers; proportional in prose

body-l.$description: Lead sentences, docs and README prose.

org.conductor.type.numeric: tabular-nums in tables, counters and timers; proportional in prose
tabular-nums in tables, counters and timers; proportional in prose

body-s.$description: Secondary lines in lists, helper text.

org.conductor.type.numeric: tabular-nums in tables, counters and timers; proportional in prose
tabular-nums in tables, counters and timers; proportional in prose
tabular-nums in tables, counters and timers; proportional in prose

overline.$description: Rare group labels. Daylight prefers sentence-case h4.

org.conductor.type.numeric: tabular-nums in tables, counters and timers; proportional in prose

numeric-l.$description: One hero number on a summary card. Fraunces has no tabular figures: never in a column.

brand.$description: The live-text wordmark beside the mark in app chrome. Matches the outlined logo.

code-s.$description: Inline ids and digests, always last on a line. The mono minimum.

size.$description: Density-dependent sizes. Comfortable is the default; compact is for operators at scale (36px rows).

control-lg.$description: Primary actions in dialogs; phone tap targets (phones always use comfortable).

table-size.$description: Font size inside tables and dense lists.

spin.$description: One turn of the running glyph. 0 = static.

sm.$description: Toasts, menus: how far things travel in.

lg.$description: Drawers start this far off their final position (plus their own width).

box.$description: Wells: code blocks and quoted logs.

badge.$description: Tags: small outlined labels. Nothing in the system is a pill.

sheet.$description: Top corners of a phone sheet.

focus.$description: Focus ring width; offset is the same.

grain.$description: The film-grain overlay on the page (decorative).

disabled.$description: Disabled controls that cannot recolour (images, charts).

breakpoint.$description: Min-widths. Phone is everything below tablet (designed at 390). CSS cannot read custom properties in media queries, so use these numbers literally.

columns.$description: Desktop and wide: 12 columns. Tablet: 8. Phone: 4.

component.$description: Component tokens: aliases of semantic tokens, so a component never knows which theme or density it is in.

fg.$description: Resting ghost text; hover and active use text.primary.

value-source.$description: The field that takes a value from Typed / Secret / Env var / Vault / Setting. Secret is the default; the others sit behind “Other source”.

ref-fg.$description: The resolved reference (secret name, env var), in mono. Ink, not accent: the accent is for things that need you.

run-strip.$description: Runs per hour, aggregated: one column per hour, stacked from the ground: passed (the soft success fill), waiting or parked (a warm neutral), running (the running blue), failed (red, on top, and marked). Replaces one lane per workflow, which does not scale.

waiting.$description: Waiting or parked runs in the strip: a warm neutral, distinct from passed in hue and, for colour-blind readers, in lightness. Not border.strong, which is below 3:1 as a data mark.
